paper.title: Offline Local Search for Online Stochastic Bandits

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic combinatorial bandits with local search ((beta,gamma)-improving moves)
unmapped: gamma-regret: compared against gamma times the optimal expected cost
generic finite feasible set X with neighborhood map N admitting (beta,gamma)-improving moves
costs are nonnegative functions cost(x,Z) of a latent i.i.d. variable Z, bounded by known C_max
learner knows C_max, max neighborhood size M, beta, gamma
only the realized total cost is observed (no semi-bandit feedback)
settings.definition_quote: we can model the cost as a function $\cost: \cX \times \cZ \to \R_+$ ... $\regret_\gamma(\cA, \cD, T) := \sum_{t=1}^T \E\left[ \cost(X_t, Z_t) \right] - \gamma \cdot T \cdot \opt$

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic completion time scheduling on a single machine (bandit feedback)
unmapped: actions are permutations of n jobs; cost is total completion time
job sizes in [0,1], possibly correlated across jobs, i.i.d. over time
settings.definition_quote: In period $t \in [T]$, the scheduler commits to a schedule $\pi^t$ before job sizes are realized according to an independent sample $P^t \sim \cD$. Then the scheduler observes $\cost(\pi^t, P^t)$, the realized total completion time of schedule $\pi^t$, but does not observe the realized job sizes $P^t$.

settings.name_in_paper: Minimum cost base of a matroid (online stochastic bandit)
unmapped: actions are bases of a matroid with ground set size n and rank r; linear cost sum of element costs
element costs jointly distributed, bounded (C_max <= r used in proof, implicitly element costs in [0,1])
settings.definition_quote: In time step $t$, given underlying realizations $z^t$, the learner observes only the cost of base $B^t$, which is $\cost(B^t, z^t) = \sum_{s\in B^t} z_s^t$.

unmapped: actions are sets of k centers from m candidates; n random points in a metric space of diameter 1
settings.definition_quote: In the bandit setting, we do not observe the realizations of the point locations. In each round $t$ a set of cluster center locations $C_t$ is submitted, after which the learner only observes $\cost(C_t,Z)$.

symbols.C_max: upper bound on realized solution costs

tuning: N_l = 3 C_max (4 log T + log M)/(delta^2 alpha^2 theta_l)

source.label: thm:gamma_regret_main_result
source.quote: Suppose that $\cX$, $\cN$, and the cost function ... admit $(\beta, \gamma)$-improving moves. Then for all distributions $\cD$ and all sufficiently large $T$, we have $\regret_\gamma(\cA_{\sf Local}, \cD, T) = O\left( \frac{M C_{\max} \log^2 T}{\delta^2 \alpha^2 \log^2 \frac{1}{\alpha}} \left( \log T + \log M \right)\right)$

results.notes: Quantity is gamma-regret (expected cost minus gamma*T*OPT), recorded as pseudo_regret with gamma-approximate benchmark. Informal Theorem 1.1 restates this.

source.label: corr_scheduling
source.quote: For any $\epsilon > 0$ there is an algorithm $\cA$ (\cref{alg:eps_regret}) with $\regret_{1+\epsilon}(\cA_, \cD, T) = O\left(\frac{n^{12} \log^3 T}{\epsilon^4 } \right).$

bound.expression_latex: O\left( \frac{ n r^6 \log^2 T}{\epsilon^4} \left(\log T + \log n \right) \right) = O\left( \frac{ n r^6 \log^3 T}{\epsilon^4} \right)

conditions: element costs bounded so that C_max <= r
tuning: beta = 1 - eps/(2r), gamma = 1+eps, circuit swap neighborhood

source.quote: Consider the problem of finding a minimum cost base in a matroid $M = (\cS, \I)$ with $|\cS| = n$ and rank $r(M)=r$ ... For any $\epsilon > 0$, there is an algorithm $\cA$ with $\regret_{1 + \epsilon}(\cA, \cD, T) = O\left( \frac{ n r^6 \log^2 T}{\epsilon^4} \left(\log T + \log n \right) \right) = O\left( \frac{ n r^6 \log^3 T}{\epsilon^4} \right).$

results.notes: Also stated as O(n r^6 log^3 T / eps^4). Covers minimum spanning trees as special case.

source.label: corr_clustering
source.quote: Consider the uncertain $k$-median clustering with candidate set of $m$ potential cluster centers where the locations of $n$ points in a metric space of diameter 1 are drawn from distribution $\cD$. There exists algorithm $\cA$ achieving $\regret_{5n/(n-1)}(\cA_, \cD, T) = O\left({n^{9}m^2\log^3 T}\right),$ when $m^2 \leq T$.
